key_insight: Reasoning-enabled LLMs can improve cybersecurity triage by learning to think through endpoint detections and calibrate confidence separately from the final label.
engineering_relevance: For SOC automation, this approach boosts high-confidence benign and malicious detection performance, making automated alert filtering more reliable.
method: Train a chain-of-thought triage classifier on human-labeled Windows endpoint detections.
Combine prompt optimization, self-training, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
Add a separate calibrator that reads the reasoning trace to estimate whether the verdict is correct.
evidence_signal: On real labeled Windows endpoint detection data, the system achieved 82.6% test accuracy and improved high-confidence benign recall by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% over a direct-label LLM classifier.
watch_item: CoT reasoning can hurt label-token probabilities used by automated triage, so confidence must be explicitly calibrated rather than inferred from the raw model output.
paper_title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models
